text:
Maya: Heads-up — since yesterday morning we've seen an uptick in preemptible evictions in us-west-2, particularly on A100-p4d-like pools. evict rate ~2.3% vs baseline 0.6% :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Jordan: Saw the same. Correlates with a large batch job launch in the region (noisy neighbor). p95 latency spikes on small-request routes.
Sam: Any chance this is transient? Do we have recent spot-price telemetry or cloud advisory?
Luis: Cloud sent a maintenance advisory for some hosts, and our spot-price anomaly detector flagged multiple reclaim events between 06:00-10:00 UTC. I attached the mini-log excerpt below:
```
2026-03-16T06:12Z reclaim host-37a - instance terminated
2026-03-16T06:13Z reclaim host-81f - migrate workloads
2026-03-16T08:47Z reclaim host-191 - abrupt
```
Grace: Impact matrix: consumer-tier routes tolerate degraded models, enterprise-tier must keep latency+SLO. Current fallback behavior fans out regionally -> if no capacity, we spill to cheaper preemptible in same region -> but that fails when region-wide churn occurs.
Maya: Proposal: 1) Add short-circuit regional failover for multi-zone churn (detect >1.5% evict across AZs) 2) Route enterprise customers to warm dedicated pool instances first, then to cross-region warm pools, then to quantized variant fallback. 3) For consumer tier allow immediate model-variant degrade (int8) + higher concurrency.
Jordan: +1 but we need to avoid double-alloc storms during failover. Suggest: ramp fanout with token-bucket and jitter, and mark requests that already saw >2 retries to use fallback variants.
Sam: Also add KV-cache preservation: when we spill across regions we should send short-lived cache tokens so downstream model warmups are faster. Otherwise p99 will tank until KV warms.
Luis: I sketched a routing policy config we could try (very small):
```
policy {
  trigger: evict_rate > 1.5%@10m
  actions: [ramp_out(2s, 20s), prefer(warm_dedicated, cross_region_warm), fallback(model_variant:int8)]
  throttle: token_bucket(rate=50/s, burst=100)
}
```
Grace: Ops questions: who owns the cross-region warm pool? cost center? we need a commit for budget because cross-region warm instances will raise steady-state spend.
Maya: Product agreed to a small reserve for high-SLA tenants last quarter — we have ~40 reserved GPUs we can tag. That should cover initial enterprise overflow for canary.
Jordan: For canary, limit to 10% of enterprise traffic and run for 2 hours, observe error budget and p99. If stable, increase to 50% and run for 24h.
Sam: What about mixed-capacity pools (mix spot + on-demand instances in same pool)? Any preference whether auto-scaler should prefer on-demand during churn?
Luis: From an implementation standpoint it's simpler to bias allocation to on-demand for enterprise tag when reclaim signals spike; keep mixed pools for consumer traffic. We can use a score function: score = capacity_cost_weight*cost + eviction_risk_weight*evict_prob. Lower score preferred.
Grace: Need cost/KPI tradeoffs documented. Can we get a quick simulation of expected monthly delta if we move 40 GPUs to cross-region warm (est +$45k/month) vs current risk of errors (estimated business impact $120k/mo at 99th pct churn)?
Maya: I'll pull numbers with finance. For immediate action: ops, can we push a limited routing patch with token-bucket ramp and model-variant fallback?
ops-bot: deploy request accepted by autoscaler:deploy-bot - rollout id r-20260316-01. Starting canary to 10% enterprise traffic to us-east-1 warm pool.
Jordan: Good. Also adding a metric flag in the rollout: metric.failover.p99 and metric.evictions.count. If either exceeds thresholds, auto-rollback.
Sam: Small checklist for rollout:
- Add token-bucket throttle to routing daemon
- Implement cache-token header for cross-region spills
- Ensure KV warmup signal is propagated to target nodes
- Canary config 10% enterprise -> us-east-1 warm pool
- Fallback variant mapping: default->quant2-int8 (latency tradeoff documented)
Luis: I'll own cache-token + KV warmup. Jordan take routing throttle. Maya own canary orchestration and comms. Grace loop in finance for budget signoff.
Maya: Timeline? Can we do a deploy in next 90m?
Jordan: I can push throttle patch in 30m, need Sam to validate KV header behavior after.
Sam: Will test in staging now. If green, I'll approve deploy.
Grace: Thanks all — please ping #oncall if any SLO breach during canary.
ops-bot: canary started (r-20260316-01) at 2026-03-16T11:05Z. Monitoring channels: infra-metrics, erroring-requests.
Maya: I'll post a short update after 1h with initial metrics.
Jordan: One more thought — add a cheap hedging strategy: spin up small spot instances in a different family as ephemeral buffer before doing cross-region spill. Lower cost than guaranteed dedicated but avoids immediate cross-region latency hit. Thoughts?
Grace: Sounds reasonable as long as we cap spend and don't create sprawl. Add to runbook.
Maya: Agreed. We'll incorporate that as step 0.
ops-bot: canary update: 15m in, evictions.count reduced by 40% for enterprise-routed requests. No p99 breach so far.
Maya: Nice. Thanks everyone, will follow up with numbers and a proposed budget tradeoff doc.
